facts.statement: Researchers created eleven new chemical compounds based on imidazolium to test if they could treat Alzheimer's disease.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The team tested how well these new compounds blocked two specific enzymes in lab experiments and computer simulations.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The majority of the new compounds stopped the enzymes more effectively than the standard drug used for comparison.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The concentration needed to block half of the acetylcholinesterase enzyme activity ranged from 21.93 to 50.58 nanomolar.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The concentration needed to block half of the butyrylcholinesterase enzyme activity ranged from 78.75 to 133.27 nanomolar.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Computer modeling showed that one specific compound, labeled 1e, fit best into the butyrylcholinesterase enzyme.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Computer modeling showed that another compound, labeled 1a, fit best into the acetylcholinesterase enzyme.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The safety and body-processing profiles of two new compounds were compared in silico to the existing drug tacrine.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The computer analysis suggests the new compounds may be more toxic to the liver and kidneys than the reference drug.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The authors state that more testing in living organisms is needed to confirm if these compounds are actually useful for treatment.
facts.subject: other
